sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2012, rev. Oct 2014. "The languages of the Tula – Waja Group". Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz (web page).
sources.note: Nothing. Tso paragraph: Tsobo (= Pire/Fire, Lotsu-Piri in Hansford et al. 1976) form a dialect cluster Bərbou / Swaabou / Gusobu (/Luuzo); 'remarkable differences between the variants foremost in the lexicon, but also phonologically'; lexical divergence from name-of-the-dead taboo. No tone or stress statement.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014. "Tula – Waja Group: Pronouns and Numbers 1-10". Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz (1 p. PDF, from field notes).
sources.note: Nothing. Tone-marked pronoun and numeral forms for Tso of Suwa (TSS) and Tso of Luuzo (TSL); no stress statement.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1995/2014. "Tula – Waja Group: 100-Wordlist". Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz (scanned PDF, 11 pp., no text layer; page 1 read as image).
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative 100-item wordlist with Tso columns (TSs Suwabou, TSg Gusubo, TSb Bərbou); forms carry tone diacritics (e.g. TSs wúlì, kúkù, búton; TSg kpát, bòùtèlòŋ), i.e. Tso is transcribed as tonal, but there is no phonological note and no mention of stress.
